title: Regulatory evidence access and encryption scope sync
summary: Redwood reviewed SOC 2 / ISO 27001 artifact access, trust center permissions, and KMS/encryption boundary for Orchard's planned Dedicated deployment. Main outcomes: confirm ability to provide time-bound access to compliance reports, outline RBAC for trust center, clarify KMS integration options (bring-your-own KMS vs Redwood-managed), and agree on a short checklist and a follow-up evidence handoff timeline.
topics: Trust Center access model and RBAC
KMS options: BYOK vs Redwood managed
Data residency implications for backups and logs
action_items: Maya Patel - Share latest Trust Center permission matrix and link to compliance pack (includes SOC 2 type II report) - Due: 2026-07-02
Devon Park - Provide list of Aruba/region requirements and preferred data residency regions - Due: 2026-07-07
Liam Chen - Run quick KV cache/batch perf estimate for Orchard sample workload and attach to the pilot doc - Due: 2026-07-05
Kevin Liu - Confirm which third party audit reports Orchard needs (SOC 2 only or ISO 27001 bundle) and share via SFTP - Due: 2026-07-06
next_steps: Redwood to send Trust Center access invite scoped to 'Compliance Review' role
Customer to confirm KMS preference (BYOK or Redwood KM) and any external HSM requirements
Schedule a 30-min demo of Dedicated admin console with full RBAC walkthrough (tentative week of 7/6)
Exchange audit evidence via secure share; Redwood to provide S3 presigned link and optional SFTP details
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sara Gomez (Orchard Head of Security), Devon Park (Orchard Platform Eng), Kevin Liu (Orchard Compliance)

Auto-summary: Quick sync to make sure Orchard can access the artifacts they need for upcoming internal audit and to nail down KMS choices for Dedicated deployment. We also walked through what the Trust Center role will let Orchard see and how audit logs are handled.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, sound and video okay?
[00:12] Sara (Orchard): Yep, can hear you. Thanks Maya.
[00:18] Liam (Redwood): I'll drive the infra bits, Maya will cover access and contract level stuff. We have about 45 minutes.
[00:27] Devon (Orchard): Great, we want to be efficient; internal audit is in mid July so hoping to get docs + access by next week if possible.
[00:35] Maya: Cool. Agenda is trust center access, SOC 2/ISO evidence delivery, RBAC mapping, and KMS options. Anything to add?
[00:44] Kevin (Orchard): Also curious about audit log retention — our policy is seven years for certain records, but we can be pragmatic.
[00:52] Maya: Noted. We'll cover retention and exports.
[01:05] Liam: Quick context — Orchard will run a Dedicated pool in us-east-1 and wants private networking. That means logs and backups could be in region; we can support region-bound storage, but we'll confirm encryption-at-rest and key handling.
[01:22] Sara: Yes, region-residency is a must for some PII processing.
[01:28] Devon: To be clear: the data that touches Redwood runtime — inference requests and KV cache metadata — needs to stay in region and we need proof of that for auditors.
[01:39] Liam: Totally. Mechanically we do not replicate across regions unless you enable cross-region backup. For Dedicated we can pin the storage to the cloud account or to a customer-managed bucket depending on the plan.
[01:53] Maya: For the trust center access, we usually provide a 'Compliance' role that can view SOC 2 reports, encryption docs, and a read-only audit log export UI. It doesn't give day-to-day admin rights.
[02:05] Sara: That's promising. How granular is the RBAC? Can we restrict to just downloading artifacts and not see runtime metrics?
[02:13] Liam: Yes, the Compliance role is scoped — it has artifact access and audit export, not metrics or cost dashboards. Slight caveat: some audit traces reference request IDs that appear in a separate tracing view, which is redacted in the compliance export.
[02:29] Kevin: That redaction is fine as long as the auditor can reconcile request IDs with our internal map.
[02:36] Maya: We'll include a small README with mappings and an example export.
[02:44] Devon: About KMS — we have corporate HSMs and prefer BYOK. Any blockers there?
[02:52] Liam: BYOK is supported. Two options: 1) Redwood-managed key wrap where you upload and rotate keys in your cloud KMS and we use that for encrypting customer buckets; or 2) Full BYOK with an HSM where you hold the root key and we perform envelope encryption. The latter needs a bit more integration work and an SCP for key usage.
[03:12] Sara: Does BYOK affect latency or supportability?
[03:16] Liam: Minimal latency impact — envelope encryption is a one-time key unwrap per session and caches keys. The main trade is operational: who rotates keys and who retains audit logs around key usage.
[03:28] Kevin: For our auditors we need usage logs showing when keys were used and by whom. Can Redwood surface that?
[03:34] Liam: We can export KMS usage logs. If you're using a cloud KMS in your account, the cloud provider's audit trail remains the source of truth; we can provide mapping and a separate Redwood audit log that shows cipher operations we triggered.
[03:47] Devon: Ok, so if we do BYOK via AWS KMS in our account, we will have CloudTrail entries that correspond. Great.
[03:54] Maya: On SOC 2 / ISO reports: we maintain a compliance pack in the Trust Center. It contains the SOC 2 Type II report, summary of controls, and a control-mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks.
[04:07] Sara: Does that mapping include evidence pointers (like where to find a proof artifact for a control)?
[04:12] Maya: Yes, it's a controls matrix with evidence pointers. There are a few items that are internal only, but we provide derivable evidence or redacted excerpts for those.
[04:23] Kevin: We need chain-of-custody for those evidence files — ideally an S3 link with time-bound presigned URLs or an SFTP transfer.
[04:31] Maya: We can do presigned S3 links with a 14-day window, or set up an SFTP dropbox for customers who require it. Which do you prefer?
[04:40] Sara: Presigned links are fine if we can lock them to the Compliance role.
[04:45] Liam: Technically the link is a direct object link; RBAC happens on the Trust Center UI so we'll send the presigned link only after we've provisioned the Compliance role.
[04:56] Devon: Can we get at least an initial set of docs before Friday? Our audit kickoff is Monday next week.
[05:02] Maya: We'll try to — I'll share what we can by Friday. Some items (like the full SOC 2 report) require an NDA or contract attachment in a couple cases — but generally for enterprise prospects we provide the standard Type II report under our existing NDA template.
[05:18] Sara: We're already under the mutual NDA from the POC conversations. That should be fine.
[05:24] Kevin: Regarding audit logs retention — our compliance team needs a retention policy confirmation: you mentioned earlier that logs are kept 2 years by default. Can that be extended?
[05:34] Liam: Default retention in Redwood hosted is 365–730 days depending on plan. For Dedicated we can configure retention and push raw logs into your on-account bucket for longer-term archival — you can then enforce your 7-year policy.
[05:48] Devon: So to be clear, we want two things: (a) real-time retention for 1 year to support triage, (b) long-term archival for 7 years in our bucket. Is that supported?
[05:58] Liam: Yes — logs are streamed to a customer-managed bucket via Kinesis or direct S3 export. We can provide the schema for the export.
[06:07] Maya: I'll attach the schema in the follow-up.
[06:12] Sara: On controls mapping — we ran a preliminary matrix and had questions about 'physical access to infrastructure' control. Since Redwood is a managed hosted vendor for this deployment, we need to show how that control is covered.
[06:25] Liam: For Dedicated in cloud, the physical control is covered by the cloud provider (e.g. AWS physical security). The mapping shows provider controls with references to their SOC 2/ISO artifacts and the sections we rely on. We'll mark those as subservice controls and show the breadcrumb.
[06:40] Kevin: Are you comfortable providing a list of subservice providers and exact control references?
[06:45] Maya: Yes, we provide a vendor list and control linkage. It's part of the compliance pack.
[06:51] Devon: A small nit — our internal auditor asked about encryption of backups. Are backups encrypted with the same KMS policy?
[06:58] Liam: Yes, backups are encrypted at rest with the same envelope logic. If you choose your own KMS, backups in your bucket will be encrypted with your key. If Redwood-managed, we use our KMS and maintain rotation and logs.
[07:11] Sara: If we go Redwood-managed keys, do we get key-usage logs for auditors?
[07:16] Liam: We'll provide Redwood-side logs for key operations. They won't be the same as CloudTrail entries tied to your account, but we can sign and timestamp those logs. For the strictest audit trail we recommend holding the key in your account.
[07:29] Kevin: That makes sense. We'll lean toward BYOK.
[07:33] Maya: Cool — we'll document the BYOK integration steps in the follow-up.
[07:39] Devon: One more question: how are PII tokens handled in logs — do you redact them automatically?
[07:46] Liam: Yes — PII redaction is configurable at ingest. We have a masking pipeline that can hash or remove fields. For compliance exports we provide a redacted version by default.
[07:57] Sara: For auditors we sometimes need reversible pseudonymization so we can re-identify under strict controls. Is that possible?
[08:04] Liam: Reversible pseudonymization is trickier in a multi-tenant managed service. If you need it, we'd recommend keeping the mapping in your account and passing hashed tokens; Redwood can accept the token and not store the mapping. We can design a flow where you hold the reversible map in your HSM or data store.
[08:22] Maya: Ok, to keep momentum let's talk about timeline: Maya will share Trust Center invite and compliance pack; Liam will provide export schemas and BYOK integration doc; customer will confirm BYOK choice and region.
[08:35] Sara: Sounds good.
[08:39] Kevin: For the evidence handoff, please include a sample control-mapping spreadsheet so our auditor knows where to look.
[08:46] Maya: We'll include that.
[08:50] Liam: Quick note on network flow diagrams — auditors often want to see flow from client to runtime to storage. We have a redacted diagram that we can share that shows VPC peering and private endpoints.
[08:59] Devon: Can you annotate it to call out where logs live and where backups land?
[09:04] Liam: Yes, I'll annotate and include it in the S3 share.
[09:10] Sara: Any blockers on legal side? Our procurement folks ask about contract-level indemnities for data residency.
[09:17] Maya: Redwood's standard enterprise addendum includes residency clauses for Dedicated deployments and S3-located backups. We'll attach a redline-ready addendum.
[09:27] Kevin: Timing on that?
[09:29] Maya: I can share a draft addendum by Friday.
[09:33] Sara: Good.
[09:36] Liam: A quick technical point: if you require air-gapped logs for certain workflows, there's an on-prem agent option that can ship only a subset of telemetry. It's more work but available.
[09:47] Devon: Not needed for this wave but good to know.
[09:51] Maya: We're at about 25 minutes in — any other big concerns?
[09:56] Sara: One small one: our auditor asked whether Redwood's SOC 2 covers the orchestration layer used in Dedicated. Does the Type II report explicitly reference Dedicated orchestration?
[10:06] Maya: The report covers our hosted control plane and core runtime. For Dedicated we have a scope note in the control matrix — some orchestration aspects are in Redwood scope, some are on the customer's cloud account. We'll flag the exact controls and supply auditor-friendly notes.
[10:21] Kevin: Excellent.
[10:25] Devon: Ok, let's talk about the evidence handoff flow step-by-step so we can include it in our internal ticket.
[10:31] Maya: Step 1: Redwood provisions Compliance role and sends invite. Step 2: Redwood uploads interim compliance pack to a presigned S3 and notifies you. Step 3: You download confirmation and we add any requested redactions. Step 4: If BYOK chosen, we run an integration checklist. Step 5: Final evidence handoff and audit support call.
[10:55] Sara: Who's the contact for the BYOK integration?
[10:59] Liam: Me (Liam). I'll coordinate with Devon on the account-level perms.
[11:04] Devon: Will need an IAM policy template.
[11:07] Liam: I'll include an example IAM policy and KMS key policy.
[11:12] Kevin: About the log schema — what fields are included by default? We need timestamps, request IDs, user identity, action, and resource. Anything else?
[11:22] Liam: Also include model-id, token counts, request latency, and a hashed user token if you enable pseudonymization. We can include raw payload if you explicitly want it, but that's opt-in.
[11:37] Sara: For the auditor we want to see how the model-id maps to deployed model versions so we can track which policy applied at time of request.
[11:45] Liam: That's in the schema; we include a model_version field.
[11:49] Maya: Ok folks, I'll recap after and post the links. Any other competitors or vendor overlaps we should be aware of?
[11:56] Kevin: Not really, this is more about matching our control set.
[12:00] Maya: Great.
[12:05] Liam: One more operational note: we support signed attestations for certain controls (evidence stamping) — if your auditor needs a signed artifact, we can provide a PGP-signed manifest for a subset of files.
[12:18] Sara: That's useful.
[12:21] Devon: Nice.
[12:24] Maya: We're at 35 minutes; any blockers to the timeline?
[12:29] Kevin: None on our side; we'll confirm BYOK choice by Monday.
[12:34] Sara: We may need a brief technical deep dive afterwards about the KMS rotation process.
[12:40] Liam: Happy to do that — 30 minutes should suffice.
[12:44] Maya: I'll set it up.
[12:47] Devon: One question I forgot: is there a way to get Delta exports for only certain resource types, not everything?
[12:54] Liam: Yes, exports support filters — you can request only auth logs, only request logs, or only admin actions. We'll include filter examples in the schema doc.
[13:05] Sara: Perfect.
[13:09] Maya: Alright wrap-up: I'll share the Trust Center invite, controls matrix, presigned link for initial docs and the addendum draft. Liam will attach KMS/IAM templates and the export schema. You (Orchard) will confirm BYOK and region selection.
[13:26] Kevin: Sounds like a plan. Thanks everyone.
[13:29] Devon: Thanks.
[13:32] Sara: Thanks, bye.

Post-call notes (auto): Transcript has intermittent speaker attribution errors in middle sections; some product names were transcribed as 'Readwood' or 'Redwood Dedicated' spelled inconsistently. Action items captured above.

References mentioned: Trust Center link (to be sent), SOC 2 Type II report, control-mapping spreadsheet, KMS integration docs, IAM policy template, network flow diagram (redacted).
